requirements.windows_path: A 26-pixel continuous-curvature (squircle) corner, not the system's circular window rounding. The stroke is an INNER stroke; a centered stroke reads a half pixel outside the curve. Glass follows OD-0005, an owner-approved deviation, not parity (see deviation): where the window shows the desktop, a Windows system material of the Acrylic class, without lensing, refraction or chromatic fringing; where the app draws its own backdrop, the full source-defined material is reproduced: shape, corner radius, tint colour and opacity, .interactive() and container spacing. This site is `.glassEffect(in: shape)`: default glass with no tint, no .interactive() and no container (DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/Chrome.swift:245, :254), so none is added. requirements.title: Command-1 to Command-9 are taken in the main window before menu dispatch, and the event is swallowed
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:5-19 the comment 'Command-1 to Command-9, taken before the event is dispatched. AppKit hands a chord that a menu item carries to the item without asking the window, and firing the item flashes its menu title, which holds the main thread for a tenth of a second on every switch.' and the monitor body `guard let self, event.window === self, attachedSheet == nil, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers) == .command, let number = Self.digitKeyCodes[event.keyCode], let selectThreadNumber else { return event }; selectThreadNumber(number); return nil`
DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:22-23 `private static let digitKeyCodes: [UInt16: Int] = [18: 1, 19: 2, 20: 3, 21: 4, 23: 5, 22: 6, 26: 7, 28: 8, 25: 9]`
DroppyCode/App/Window/WindowManager.swift:64-65 the main window's selectThread and selectThreadNumber closures are wired to model.selectThread(offset:) and model.selectThread(number:)
requirements.preconditions: The main window is key, no sheet is attached to it, and the digit closure has been installed.
requirements.action: The user presses Command and a number-row digit from 1 to 9.
requirements.expected_result: The nth thread in the sidebar's order is selected and the event is consumed, so the matching menu item never fires and its title never flashes. Every one of the five conditions is required: the event must belong to this window, no sheet may be attached, the masked modifier set must be exactly Command and nothing else, the key code must be one of the nine, and the closure must be installed. Failing any of them the event is returned unchanged and follows its normal route. Note the key code map's crossover: 23 is digit 5 and 22 is digit 6.
requirements.windows_path: A pre-translate keyboard hook on the main window that runs before accelerator dispatch, testing VK_1..VK_9 (not the numpad) with the masked modifier set exactly equal to Ctrl. It must consume the message so the menu command does not also fire. The macOS reason for the interception (a flashing menu title costing a tenth of a second) may not apply, but the double-fire it prevents does.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: Command-3 selects the third thread once, not twice; unit over the nine key codes including the 22/23 crossover

requirements.preconditions: The main window exists.
requirements.action: The selectThreadNumber closure is assigned, possibly more than once.
requirements.expected_result: A single monitor is installed on the first non-nil assignment and is kept for the process lifetime. A second assignment does not install a second monitor, so the digit chord never fires twice. Nothing removes it, which is intentional because the main window is created once.
requirements.windows_path: Install the hook once per main window and hold it for the window's lifetime. Guard against a second installation, and unhook when the window is finally destroyed even though the source does not, since a leaked Windows hook is a process-wide cost rather than a per-app one; record that as a deliberate, safe divergence.

requirements.title: The main window answers the next and previous thread chords itself, but only for the Tab key
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:25-38 `override func performKeyEquivalent(with event: NSEvent) -> Bool { if event.keyCode == 48, attachedSheet == nil { let chord = KeyChord(keyCode: Int(event.keyCode), modifiers: event.modifierFlags); if chord == ShortcutStore.shared.chord(for: .nextThread) { selectThread?(1); return true }; if chord == ShortcutStore.shared.chord(for: .previousThread) { selectThread?(-1); return true } }; return super.performKeyEquivalent(with: event) }`
requirements.preconditions: The main window is key and no sheet is attached.
requirements.action: The user presses a Tab chord, by default Control-Tab or Control-Shift-Tab.
requirements.expected_result: If the chord matches the live next-thread chord the selection moves down one; if it matches the previous-thread chord it moves up one; either way the event is consumed. The window handles this ONLY for key code 48 (Tab): a user who rebinds next thread to a non-Tab chord falls through to the ordinary menu route instead. The chords are read live from the shortcut store, so a remap of a Tab chord is honored here too. Next is tested before previous, so if both are bound to the same chord next wins.
requirements.windows_path: Handle VK_TAB chords on the main window before the frameworks consume Tab for focus navigation, which they otherwise do. Keep the key-code gate: a rebound non-Tab chord must reach the ordinary command route. Keep the next-before-previous order.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with the defaults and after rebinding next thread to a non-Tab chord

requirements.title: A secondary window closes on Escape, unless a text field has focus
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/Window/ThreadWindow.swift:41-56 the class comment and `override func sendEvent(_ event: NSEvent) { if event.type == .keyDown, event.keyCode == 53, event.modifierFlags.intersection(KeyChord.allowedModifiers).isEmpty, !(firstResponder is NSText) { performClose(nil); return }; super.sendEvent(event) }` with the comment 'Escape closes it as well, like a sheet. Taken here rather than in keyDown, which the SwiftUI hosting view never passes on. A field being typed in keeps its Escape, and a shortcut being recorded takes it before any window sees it.'
requirements.preconditions: A secondary window, in practice the Settings window, is key.
requirements.action: The user presses Escape with no modifiers.
requirements.expected_result: The window closes, exactly as a sheet would. Escape is NOT taken when any modifier is held, nor while the focused responder is a text field, which keeps Escape for the field itself. requirements.preconditions: A drag region is drawn over a stretch of chrome.

If O-68 later shows macOS does not zoom on double-click, swallow WM_NCLBUTTONDBLCLK for these regions in the ED-063 hook.

requirements.title: A drag handle taken out of its window mid-drag clears its drag state and pops a pushed drag cursor, but does NOT call onEnd
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:127-133 viewDidMoveToWindow: `if window == nil, isDragging { isDragging = false; if dragCursor != nil { NSCursor.pop() } }` - no call to onEnd or onChange
DroppyCode/App/Views/Chat/SubagentPanel.swift:724-731 (B2) - the only place this state was previously covered, in the panel's own PanelDragHandleView, before N8 shares it
requirements.preconditions: A drag handle is mid-drag (isDragging true) when its view is removed from its window - for example the drawer or panel it belongs to is dismissed or toggled closed while the mouse button is still held.
requirements.action: The handle's view leaves its window.
requirements.expected_result: isDragging is cleared to false and, if a dragCursor was pushed for this drag, it is popped. Critically, onEnd is NOT called and onChange is not called with a final delta: whatever the caller does in onEnd (Terminal commits terminalHeight and clears isTerminalResizing; the sidebar strip commits its width) does not run. A caller that only commits state in onEnd can therefore be left in a stuck intermediate state after this happens.
side_effects: A pushed cursor is popped
The caller's onEnd/onChange side effects (a settings commit, a flag reset) do NOT run
requirements.persistence: Whatever onEnd would have written is NOT written.
failure_cases: A caller relying on onEnd for cleanup (clearing a busy flag, committing a value) must handle this path separately, since it will not fire here
requirements.cancellation: not applicable; this IS the cancellation-like path
requirements.windows_path: When a drag handle's control is detached from its visual tree or moved to a different window mid-drag, clear the drag state and release any captured pointer/pushed cursor, but do not invoke the completion callback. Record this as a pre-existing port gap where the current implementation calls end() on capture loss instead (6.2): TerminalPanel's capture-lost path must be corrected to match this record, not the other way around.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test: start a drag, then remove the handle's window (or dismiss the panel) while still holding the mouse button; assert onEnd was never called and isDragging is false afterward
requirements.b3_note: New shared behaviour at B3 (DragHandle.swift:127-133), part of N8. At B2 only PanelDragHandleView (SubagentPanel.swift:724-731) had this; TERM's TerminalPanel never did, and its own new-record proposal for this (R3-12 #2) explicitly says it belongs with DragHandle.swift's records, folded here. requirements.title: DragHandleView's component contract: axis travel signs, grip and glow defaults, the 0.18 s/4 pt metrics, slop gating, and cursor-identity invalidation
source_evidence: DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:257-266 travel(to:) - `.horizontal`: `CGSize(width: point.x - pressOrigin.x, height: 0)`; `.vertical`: `CGSize(width: 0, height: point.y - pressOrigin.y)`; `.free`: `CGSize(width: point.x - pressOrigin.x, height: pressOrigin.y - point.y)` (y inverted, running down like a panel offset, unlike the other two axes which run up)
DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:18-30 Grip defaults: alpha 0.6, hoverGlow 0.05, dragGlow 0.10, glowInset nil, refreshesHoverOnLayout false
DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:58-61 Metrics: glowRadius 4, duration 0.18

DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:198-220 slop gating in mouseDown/mouseDragged: with slop 0, isDragging becomes true and onBegin fires on mouseDown itself; with slop > 0, mouseDown leaves isDragging false, and mouseDragged waits until `abs(travel.width) >= slop || abs(travel.height) >= slop` before setting isDragging true and firing onBegin

DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:39-44 `var cursor: NSCursor = .arrow { didSet { guard cursor !== oldValue else { return }; window?.invalidateCursorRects(for: self) } }` - identity comparison, not equality, and a cursor rect invalidation only on an actual change

DroppyCode/UI/Chrome/DragHandle.swift:104-114 configure(grip:): `if !hasConfigured || hadGrip != (grip != nil) { hasConfigured = true; updateGrip(animated: false) }` - a re-render (SwiftUI re-applying the same or a changed configuration) does not itself call updateGrip unless this is the first configuration or the grip's presence toggled, so a running hover or drag animation is never snapped mid-flight by an unrelated re-render
requirements.preconditions: None; a component-level contract every DragHandle instance follows regardless of its caller.
requirements.action: Any DragHandle is configured, dragged, or re-rendered.
requirements.expected_result: Travel is reported in the axis's own terms: horizontal reports x only, vertical reports y only (positive means up, i.e. AppKit's native sense), and free reports both with y inverted to run down, matching a panel's own offset convention. Grip defaults (usable without setting every field) are alpha 0.6, hoverGlow 0.05, dragGlow 0.10, no glow (glowInset nil) and no layout-driven hover re-read (refreshesHoverOnLayout false); Sidebar overrides glowInset and refreshesHoverOnLayout, Terminal overrides neither. Every grip's animation, when animated, runs 0.18 s ease-out; a glow's corner radius is always 4. A handle with slop 0 (Sidebar, Terminal) starts dragging on press; a handle with slop > 0 (none exist yet, but the mechanism supports it) waits for that much combined travel first. Setting `cursor` to the same NSCursor instance is a no-op (identity check); an actual change invalidates the window's cursor rects so the new cursor takes effect without waiting for the next mouse move. Reconfiguring a handle with the same or a compatibly-present grip never interrupts a hover or drag animation already in flight.
requirements.cancellation: not applicable; this is a static contract
requirements.windows_path: Port this as the shared DragHandleView/DragHandle component's own contract, independent of any one caller: the axis travel signs (free's y-inversion is easy to get backwards, and SubagentPanel.cs:908-913 already has this exact sign bug pre-existing at B2, per 6.2), the grip/glow defaults, the 0.18 s/4 pt metrics, slop as a configurable threshold even though no current caller sets it above 0, cursor-identity-based invalidation (not value equality), and animation continuity across re-renders.
requirements.verification_method: unit: travel signs for each axis, including a regression test for the free-axis y-inversion; the default field values; slop 0 versus slop > 0 gating; setting the same cursor instance twice does not re-invalidate; reconfiguring mid-animation does not reset it
requirements.b3_note: New component-level record for the new shared unit UI.Chrome.DragHandle (N8), which did not exist as a separate, independently specified component at B2 (its behaviour was duplicated inline in WindowChrome.swift's SidebarResizeHandleView and TerminalPanel.swift's TerminalResizeHandleView). From impacts.json R3-28's new_records_needed #3.

ui.notes: The 16-point label clamp exists so a monospaced command does not draw a taller capsule than a plain "Sign in" beside it. This site is `.buttonStyle(.glass)` (DroppyCode/App/Views/RootView.swift:448), so the glass button style is kept, with its label held to 16 points. UNK-0004 is closed by that ruling.
